Title: VTES Survivor Format - different game format.

Messages.Author: Damien Hennessy
Messages.Body:
I can hear the groans already :-)

My group was playing around with different game varients, just to try
out different things and see how they work.

I present the Vtes/Jyhad Survivor Format:

The rules, nothing changes. Everything stays the same except you don't
chose one deck, you pick 2-5 decks. (Depending on how long you feel
like taking)

Now, lets assume we have for players A, B, C, D.

Each player has chosen two decks for the Surviror format.

The seating order is done as normal and you play as normal. Let's
assume the seating order is like this.

A > D > B > C

Now A ousts D.

A > B > C

B has a turn as normal, C has a turn as normal and take actions
against A.

D re-enters play with a second deck, taking A's old position. So now
the table seating is like this.

D > A > B > C

D's turn runs as normal except that in this one turn D gets ten
transfer points in that one influence phase.

So A now has D behind him.

A's turn. Play resumes as normal until someone else is outsed.

So far the format works pretty well, (1VP per deck kill). You still
gain six pool for ousting a player/deck.

Notes:

Only real problem is people shifting stuff around, through if you have
a decent sized table this isn't too much of an issue. We have only
tried this format in 2, 3 and 4 player games to decent success.

I looking on improving this idea so any feedback, questions, etc are
most welcome.

:-)

Then, if I understand correctly, we now have a player who for some reason
was the first to be ousted, and he gets in the game with 30 pool and 10
transfer, at a time when the other meths will probably be much weaker.
You'll object : "yes but they too, if killed, will come back". It is worse
IMO : we get a game looking way too much like randomness to me.

It can also be abused. My second deck is a weenie. I begin my second turn
with 4 minions who bleed a weakened meth for a disciplineless 6-8 pool, or a
dominate *much more* (stealthed or not, does it really matter ?). Not
counting the obvious Anarch Revolt. This is just an example on top of my
head, the meaning being : the second and subsequent decks can be calculated
for these precise rules.

Of course, if you find this format fun, do whatever you want. But I don't
think this game looks anymore like VTES : too many unbalancing factors.

Messages.Author: Damien Hennessy
Messages.Body:
>
> Then what?
>
> How and when does a game end?
>
> Is there a limit on how many times a player can be ousted and keep coming back in?
>
> Does only the first guy out get to come back, or everybody?
>

An ousted player can keep coming back as long as he has decks. You use
your first deck and then when you are ousted, you pull out your second
deck. When ousted a second time you are gone (or if you have more
decks).

The rule applies to everybody.

You may only come back as long as you have decks.

As pointed out, many things seem godawfully strong in this format.
The easy solution is - play a universal hoser deck first (AR, for
instance), let yourself be ousted first, then come back with a massive
bloat machine. You're back with your second deck while everyone else
is weakly struggling to hang on with their first. You build and build
and build, until eventually the others just have to die. Then you're
essentially starting a new game, only you're starting with twice as
much pool.

> I'd play this variant with 12 gehenna cards per deck. You're welcome to
> influence out that 1-capacity Arika who can do nothing but hunt. ;-)

Actually, Gehenna doesn't really work in this format. They still have
the "once per game" limitation. Once the methusaleh who controls the
events is ousted, no one can ever play those events again.
